section banner: Load and prepare data

spans.operation: pick the source CSV and load the full raw dyad-level dataset with no row filtering
collapse the two raters' skin-tone scores into a single measure by averaging them
bucket the continuous skin-tone score into Light/Medium/Dark using cutpoints 0.25 and 0.625
collapse the red-card count into a yes/no indicator for whether any red card occurred in the dyad
fold the many raw position labels into four buckets (Goalkeeper/Defender/Forward/Midfielder) via keyword matching
quantify how well the two raters agree, via Pearson correlation and exact-match rate, on the non-missing subset
restrict the working sample to dyads with complete data on skin tone category, position, height and weight, dropping everything else

spans.note: print sample size, unique player/referee counts, and skin tone distribution
compute and print unadjusted red-card summary by skin tone category

spans.operation: one-hot encode position and league without dropping a reference column at the get_dummies step
z-score height and weight before putting them in the model
log-transform the games-played count instead of using it raw

assemble the regression design matrix: encode skin tone as Dark/Medium indicators with Light left as reference, pick which position and league dummies enter (Defender and one league omitted as reference), and choose the final covariate set alongside the binary outcome
fit a logistic regression as the outcome model, with standard errors clustered on player rather than left unclustered

define the primary effect as a covariate-adjusted risk difference: hold every other covariate at its sample mean (0 for the standardized ones) and contrast predicted P(red card) for Dark vs Light skin tone

spans.note: print adjusted probabilities and risk difference

spans.operation: quantify uncertainty on the predicted probabilities via a parametric bootstrap (10,000 draws from the coefficient sampling distribution), using the percentile method for the CI and a two-sided proportion-based p-value

spans.note: print bootstrap CI and p-value for risk difference

spans.operation: report a secondary effect as an adjusted odds ratio, with its CI built from a Wald normal-approximation around the log-odds coefficient rather than the bootstrap

spans.note: print adjusted odds ratio, CI, p-value

spans.operation: re-estimate the same model clustering standard errors by referee instead of player, and recompute the bootstrap risk-difference CI/p-value under that alternative clustering
